# configdirector_config (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    configdirector = {
      source  = "ConfigDirector/configdirector"
      version = "~> 0.8"
    }
  }
}

provider "configdirector" {}

resource "configdirector_project" "example" {
  name = "Config Example"
  slug = "config-example"
}

resource "configdirector_tag" "payments" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  name       = "Payments / EU & US"
}

# A simple boolean flag - the most common case.
resource "configdirector_config" "new_checkout_flow" {
  project_id  = configdirector_project.example.id
  key         = "new-checkout-flow"
  description = "Enables the redesigned checkout flow."
  role        = "flag"
  type        = "boolean"
  tags        = [configdirector_tag.payments.name]

  # Write-only: the API never returns a config's default value, and
  # changing it after creation is a no-op - it can only be set at create
  # time. Ongoing default value changes go through
  # configdirector_config_targeting_rules instead (see that resource's
  # example).
  initial_value = false
}

# A kill-switch, visible to both client and server SDKs (the default for
# both, shown explicitly here).
resource "configdirector_config" "maintenance_mode" {
  project_id  = configdirector_project.example.id
  key         = "maintenance-mode"
  description = "Puts the app into maintenance mode when enabled."
  role        = "kill-switch"
  type        = "boolean"
  client      = true
  server      = true
  tags        = []

  initial_value = false
}

# An integer config, bounded via type_options. type_options is shaped
# differently depending on "type" (see the resource documentation for the
# other shapes) and isn't validated by Terraform - it's passed through
# as-is and validated by the API.
resource "configdirector_config" "max_upload_size_mb" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  key        = "max-upload-size-mb"
  role       = "config"
  lifetime   = "permanent"
  type       = "integer"

  type_options = {
    isInteger = true
    min = {
      relation = ">="
      value    = 1
    }
    max = {
      relation = "<="
      value    = 500
    }
  }

  initial_value = 25
}

# An enum config, restricted to a fixed set of values via type_options.
resource "configdirector_config" "checkout_theme" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  key        = "checkout-theme"
  role       = "config"
  lifetime   = "permanent"
  type       = "enum"

  type_options = {
    valueType = "string"
    values    = ["classic", "modern", "minimal"]
  }

  initial_value = "classic"
}

resource "configdirector_metric" "subscription_started" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  event_name = "subscription_started"
  direction  = "higher-is-better"
  kinds      = ["conversion"]
}

# An experiment with named variations - see
# configdirector_config_targeting_rules for how traffic actually gets split
# between them. Its metrics say what the results measure, and its hypothesis
# what the team expects; each run keeps the hypothesis it started with.
resource "configdirector_config" "pricing_experiment" {
  project_id = configdirector_project.example.id
  key        = "pricing-experiment"
  role       = "experiment"
  type       = "string"
  hypothesis = "A lower price gets more customers to subscribe."

  variations = [
    { name = "Control", value = "control" },
    { name = "Higher Price", value = "higher-price" },
    { name = "Lower Price", value = "lower-price" },
  ]

  metrics = [
    { metric_id = configdirector_metric.subscription_started.id, role = "primary", primary_kind = "conversion" },
  ]

  initial_value = "control"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `initial_value` (Dynamic) Default value used when creating this config - a plain string, number, or bool matching "type". Despite the name, this isn't reconciled on every apply the way most attributes are: the ConfigDirector API has no endpoint that returns the global default back, so it's write-only from Terraform's perspective, sent only on create. Changing it after the config already exists never replaces the resource and never reaches the API - the stored value is pinned to whatever was set at create time. Note this only stops the *value* from drifting: Terraform will still show a pending update (and this provider will still make a no-op API call) on every plan/apply for as long as the configured value disagrees with the pinned one. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [initial_value] }` on the resource to suppress that too. Ongoing default value changes go through per-environment targeting rules instead, which aren't modeled by this resource yet. Exception: right after import, there's nothing yet to pin to (import can't populate this attribute either - see ImportState), so the first apply adopts whatever's configured as the new baseline instead of conflicting with it.
- `key` (String)
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project this config belongs to.
- `role` (String) What the config is for: "config" (a general value), "flag" (a feature flag), "kill-switch" or "experiment". A flag can become a kill switch and a kill switch a flag; the config is updated in place and its lifetime follows the new role. Any other role change fails the plan.
- `type` (String)

### Optional

- `client` (Boolean)
- `description` (String)
- `hypothesis` (String) What the team expects the variations to do, up to 1,000 characters. Only an experiment has a hypothesis. Each run keeps the hypothesis as it was when the run started, so changing it changes neither earlier runs nor the run in progress. Omit to keep the current hypothesis; set "" to remove it.
- `lifetime` (String) "temporary" for a config you expect to remove, which ConfigDirector tracks through its lifecycle, or "permanent". The role decides it for every role but "config": a flag or an experiment is always temporary and a kill switch always permanent, so leave it out for those; a value that contradicts the role fails the plan. A config with the "config" role needs a lifetime when it is created; leaving it out later keeps the lifetime it has.
- `metrics` (Attributes Set) The metrics an experiment measures, unordered: up to 10, at most one of them primary. Only an experiment has metrics. Omit to keep the metrics attached in the dashboard or elsewhere, during unrelated updates and after import; set [] to detach every metric. A set of metrics manages exactly those and corrects attachment drift. Creating an experiment with metrics attaches them in a second request once the experiment exists; when that request fails, the experiment is replaced on the next apply. Attaching metrics requires config-settings:update. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metrics))
- `server` (Boolean)
- `tags` (Set of String) Unordered assigned tag names, resolved within this project's catalog. Omit to preserve remote assignments after import, during unrelated updates, or when relinquishing ownership; set [] to clear all. An explicit nonempty set detects and corrects assignment drift. Names must already exist; assignment never creates tags. Reference configdirector_tag.<name>.name for creation and rename ordering. Equivalent names share one assignment and retain configured spelling while the assigned tag IDs are unchanged. Resolving names requires tags:read; creating a config, tagged or not, requires configs:create; changing assignments requires config-settings:update. Reads and data sources show assigned names under configs:read alone.
- `type_options` (Dynamic) Type-specific options for this config, shaped differently depending on "type" (e.g. min/max for integer/float, values for enum, unit for timespan). Not validated by Terraform - the structure you provide is passed through as-is and validated by the API.
- `variations` (Dynamic) Per-variation values for this config, as a list of {name, value} objects. Only valid when role is "experiment"; the API rejects it (and this provider validates it client-side) for any other role. Not validated by Terraform beyond that - the structure you provide is passed through as-is and validated by the API.

### Read-Only

- `deprecated_keys` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--deprecated_keys))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `state` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--metrics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metrics`

Optional:

- `metric_id` (String) Required in each metric: the id of a configdirector_metric in the config's project.
- `primary_kind` (String) The kind the primary metric decides on, one of the kinds its metric reports: "conversion", "count-per-context" or "value-per-context". Only the primary metric has one.
- `role` (String) Required in each metric: "primary" for the metric and kind that decide the experiment, "secondary" for supporting evidence, or "guardrail" for a metric that must not get worse.


<a id="nestedatt--deprecated_keys"></a>
### Nested Schema for `deprecated_keys`

Read-Only:

- `config_id` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `is_primary` (Boolean)
- `key` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Note: initial_value can't be recovered by import - see import.sh for why.
import {
  to = configdirector_config.new_checkout_flow
  id = "config-example/new-checkout-flow"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id_or_slug>/<key> - the project half accepts either its UUID or
# its slug.
#
# Note: initial_value can't be recovered by import - the API never returns
# a config's default value, so it reads as unset afterward, and the first
# apply following import adopts whatever's configured as the new baseline
# rather than actually changing anything remotely. Make sure it's set to
# the value you want treated as the baseline going forward before that
# first apply.
terraform import configdirector_config.new_checkout_flow config-example/new-checkout-flow
```
